response:
I wrote this as a single `company-handbook` skill, but not exactly as asked. Pasting 3,000 lines into SKILL.md with the description "Use for anything related to our company" breaks the skill-building rules in two ways:

- **Description:** it has no trigger phrase and no instruction, so it tells Claude neither when to activate nor what to do. The description is the only part always in context, and a catch-all one makes the skill fire on everything or nothing.
- **Body size:** 3,000 lines almost certainly exceeds the body character cap. It would also load all seven topics every time, when most requests need one.

This version still gives one skill and one entry point. The content lives in `references/` files that load only when needed, so the pasting is the same amount of work.

## SKILL.md

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Invoke when asked about company code style, deploys or rollbacks, on-call alerts, PTO or expenses, brand voice, org contacts, or internal terms. Read the matching reference file first; answer from it, not from memory.
---

# Company Handbook

Find the topic below, read only that reference file, then answer from it.

## Routing

| If the request is about | Read |
|---|---|
| Python or TypeScript style, lint, naming | [code-style.md](references/code-style.md) |
| Deploying any of the 4 services, rollback | [deploy.md](references/deploy.md) |
| A firing alert or on-call action | [oncall-runbook.md](references/oncall-runbook.md) |
| PTO, expenses, reimbursement | [pto-expenses.md](references/pto-expenses.md) |
| Marketing copy, tone, brand voice | [brand-voice.md](references/brand-voice.md) |
| Who owns what, who to contact | [org-chart.md](references/org-chart.md) |
| Unfamiliar internal term or acronym | [glossary.md](references/glossary.md) |

## Rules

- Read one reference at a time; do not load all of them.
- If a reference does not cover the question, say so rather than guessing.
- For deploys and alerts, quote the exact steps from the file and keep their order.
```

## references/ layout (paste your existing content here)

- `code-style.md` (~600 lines): split into Python and TypeScript sections, with a short ToC.
- `deploy.md` (~400 lines): one section per service, with a Rollback subsection under each.
- `oncall-runbook.md` (~900 lines): one heading per alert type (35), each with Symptom, Check, Action. Add a ToC listing all 35 so Claude can jump to the right one. If it grows, split by service.
- `pto-expenses.md` (~300 lines): PTO and expenses as separate sections.
- `brand-voice.md` (~250 lines): voice principles, do/don't examples.
- `org-chart.md` (~200 lines): see the note below.
- `glossary.md` (~350 lines): alphabetical, one term per heading or line.

## Things to flag to your lead

1. **Phone numbers in the org chart.** Personal contact details in a file that gets packaged and loaded into model context are a privacy and leak risk. I'd keep names, roles, and ownership in `org-chart.md` and link to the HR directory or on-call tool for phone numbers.
2. **Stale content.** On-call and deploy docs change often. If these files copy a canonical source, add a "last verified" date to each file or link to the source.
3. **Not validated.** I didn't run `validate.py`, so check the frontmatter and size limits with `python3 scripts/validate.py company-handbook` before packaging. The skill guidance also asks for 3+ test cases in `evals/evals.json`. For example: "how do I roll back the billing service?", "what's the PTO carryover rule?", and "what does alert X mean?".

If your lead wants a hard "knows everything" guarantee, the routing table is where to add rows as the handbook grows, with no changes to the description.
